syllabus_topics: Basic concepts of continuous-time (CT) and discrete-time (DT) signals. Examples. Transformations.
Basic concepts of systems. Memory, causality, invariance, linearity, stability, invertibility.
Linear time-invariant systems (LTI systems). Unit impulse response. Convolution. Properties.
Fourier series (FS) of CT signals. Exponentials as eigenfunctions of LTI systems. Representation of periodic signals in FS.
Fourier transform (FT) of CT signals. Representation of aperiodic signals via FT. Frequency response, filtering.
Fourier transform of DT signals. Concept of DT signal spectrum. LTI systems described by difference equations.
Sampling. DT processing of CT signals. Sampling theorem. Aliasing.
Laplace transform (LT). Transfer function (TF). LTI systems described by differential equations, poles and zeros. Block diagrams and equivalent TFs. Unilateral LT.
assessment_rules: The final grade NF = 0.4L + 0.6E, rounded to the nearest integer, with additional approval conditions L>=7.5 and E>=8. For special examination periods, and for student workers who have not completed the laboratory work, the final grade is solely based on the exam: NF=E. Final grades above 18 will require an additional oral examination. During exams, consultation of transform tables and a one-page (A4, front and back) handwritten formula sheet is allowed, as is the use of a calculator.
